content:
Apple's first foldable iPhone is expected to make its official debut in just over a week. Reports indicate that during the development phase, Apple internally considered launching a brand-new Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra, but this stylus is almost certainly never going to actually hit the market.

The information comes from Bloomberg reporter Mark Gurman, who specifically emphasised that this Apple Pencil will not be unveiled next month. However, he still described in detail the original appearance design and expected operation method of this stylus.

This stylus was originally designed to be different from the Apple Pencil currently used in the iPad lineup; its design is shorter to match the shorter body proportions of the iPhone Ultra. However, similar to the iPad version of the Apple Pencil, it was originally designed to magnetically attach to the side of the device for easy storage and charging.

He pointed out that holding this stylus while using the iPhone Ultra would be quite awkward, because the stylus would be attached to the side of the device; by contrast, when using an iPad in landscape mode, the stylus attaches to the top.

He also mentioned that this stylus would very likely leave "unsightly marks" on the more fragile inner screen of the iPhone Ultra.

He ultimately speculated that the main reason Apple decided not to release this stylus was that it did not want to go against the stance Steve Jobs坚持 when he unveiled the original iPhone — "Who wants a stylus?"

Personally, I still think an Apple Pencil designed specifically for the iPhone Ultra would be quite practical, but it looks like we won't be seeing this stylus anytime soon.

Following the recent round of price hikes, it might be worth keeping an eye on Apple's refurbished product store — you might just find a great deal, as various refurbished products can save quite a bit of money, including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple Watch and Apple TV.
